title: Hollerhorn Distilling Rauch
about: Hollerhorn Distilling sits on a hillside outside Naples, the old grape village at the south end of Canandaigua Lake. Karl Neubauer, a Naples native and longtime custom home builder, studied distilling for some fifteen years before he and his wife Melissa opened in 2018, in a building Karl framed from timber salvaged out of collapsing barns. A fire in May 2022 destroyed the tasting room, but the stills and barrels survived, and the couple rebuilt with help from the whole valley. Karl works almost entirely with fruit and grain grown within a short drive of the distillery.

Rauch is German for smoke. Hollerhorn gives many of its spirits German names, from Pflaume (plum) and Kirsch (cherry) to Erdbeer (strawberry) and Weintraube (grape), and smoke is one of Karl Neubauer’s signatures: his Flamed Maple rests in a cask charred with Scottish peat, The Darkening is built on peated New York malt, and Etheryeal is a rye vodka made with peat-smoked malt.
Rauch is one of the distillery’s newest, smallest releases, and Hollerhorn has not yet published its details. Ask your server about what is in the glass tonight.
